overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the minutes complaint, declined the recording and conduct complaint as not OML violations, and declined the claim against the Interim Town Administrator. No remedy was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged minutes of the Aug 22, Sep 6 and Sep 19 executive sessions were insufficient because they did not capture discussion of complaints against three police officers.
allegations.key_passage: After review of the August 22, September 6, and September 19 executive session minutes, we find that all three sets of minutes, with respect to the discussions at issue in this complaint, are sufficient to comply with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Aug 15 and Oct 3 executive session minutes were insufficient for the same reason; the AG declined review of both sets.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review again whether the original August 15 minutes were insufficient.

allegations.summary: Not alleged by complainant; the AG noted on its own that the Aug 22 and Sep 6 notices cited the original purpose rather than stating a review of prior minutes.
allegations.key_passage: A public may cite to either the original executive session purpose or G.L. c. 30A, § 21(a)(7) (“Purpose 7”), citing to the Open Meeting Law, when convening in executive session to review executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged recordings of the Sep 6 and Sep 19 executive sessions were posted online, which they said was improper.
Complainant alleged Board members made derogatory comments about them that were captured in the posted executive session recordings.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, an allegation of unprofessional conduct or incivility towards a member of the public does not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Interim Town Administrator violated the Open Meeting Law, but that individual is not a public body or member acting as one.
